title: Type and log the catch block in TutorPinResetScreen._sendResetEmail
why: The bare `catch (e)` has no `on X` type, so per Dart semantics it catches everything thrown — including Error subtypes (StateError, TypeError, NoSuchMethodError from a programmer bug) — and silently converts all of them into the same generic 'send failed' UI message with zero AppLogger call. A real programming defect elsewhere in the call chain would present identically to a normal network failure, with no trace to diagnose it.
recommendation: Catch a specific exception type (or at least log via AppLogger.instance.error before setting the UI message) so Error subtypes are not silently masked and failures are traceable.
acceptance_criteria: the catch block logs via AppLogger with the exception and stack trace before updating _errorMessage
the catch is narrowed to typed exceptions the send/clear operations can actually throw, not a bare catch(e)
